body.statement: For every \(n\ge2M\), \(\mathsf K_n\) acts on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) by \(\lambda_{n,k}=(-1)^k(M)_k/(n-M)_k\). Consequently, for centered \(f,g\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) and a uniform ordered disjoint pair \((A,C)\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(f(A),g(C))=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}\langle\Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,k}g\rangle_n\), and \(C_{\tau\tau,n}=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}\|\Pi_{n,k}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2\).
body.justification: This identity converts the global dependence from disjoint group formation into auditable harmonic energies with exact signs and finite-sample constants.
body.gap: Filmus2016, Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion, supplies the common eigenspaces, while BrouwerEtAl2018 supplies the classical Kneser spectrum; neither derives a causal design variance for random groups.
body.consumer: The identity is the input for the dense PAME variance correction and every subsequent comparison with CR2.
